recs.x: distributions in the real world. Average is useful for more than just Gaussian, but it means different things in different distributions, most of them quite unlike what our Gaussian-trained intuition suggests. Standard deviation is really Gaussian-only, or at least, if you insist on using it, you ought to pair it with the skew, kurtosis, or other measures of how non-Gaussian your distribution is. Remembering that there's only one way to be Gaussian but an infinity of ways to be non-gaussian is helpful too. This can be a helpful video to visualize that: [link]
